(By Sri.K.R.S., Adv.,)
 Judgment

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest from date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of Sri.Danush.S, who succumbed to injuries in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 03.04.2024 at about 2.30 p.m., the deceased Danush.S was proceeding as a pillion rider in Bajaj Pulsar motor bike, bearing Reg.no.AP-03-CP-3277 on Punganur-Palamanur Highway Road.
The said vehicle was driven by rider of the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner at Gudurupalle turning and lost control over his vehicle.
Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Punganur Govt. Hospital in 108 Ambulance wherein first-aid treatment and then referred to Bright Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and later he succumbed to the injuries on 06.05.2024.
The petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical treatment, transportation of body, funeral and other expenses.

4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased Danush.S was very hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and he was working as Painter and earning Rs.30,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have came to stand still.

The petitioner No.1 is mother of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the brother of the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have became miserable and hence this petition.
5. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
6. After registration of the petition.
Notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, he has been placed exparte.
However, the respondent No.2 has appeared before this court and has filed written statement on its behalf and denying the entire petition averments.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied Dhanalakshmi G J vs Ganesh M on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197841946/
2 the age, avocation and income of the deceased.

7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner No.1 herself is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.

The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
8.
I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Danush.S died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.04.2024 at about 2.30 p.m., on Punganur Road, NH-42 ATY Gudurupalle Turning, Punganur Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligence riding of the Bajaj Pulsar Motor bike bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CP-3277 by its rider?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative.

Partly in the affirmative,

The said vehicle was driven by rider of the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner at Gudurupalle turning and lost control over his vehicle.
Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries in hospital.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.

Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 125(a)

Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report.
Ex.P.2 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the rider of the offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CP-3277.
The PW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for respondents.
During the course of cross-examination of petitioner nothing was elicited from their mouth, so as to disbelieve his version.
The Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
RW.1 has reiterated the contents of written statement filed by the respondent No.2 in his examination in chief.

RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for petitioner during the course of cross- examination of petitioner he had admitted that he has deposed his evidence on the basis of documents submitted by him.
He does not have any personal knowledge about the case.
The policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident.
The said policy is a comprehensive policy which included third party insurance coverage for two wheeler vehicle.
The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of our insured vehicle.

13. Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that the respondents have admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CP-3277.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CP- 3277.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 14.
The PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that, her deceased son Danush. S was working as Painter and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
His son was aged about 22 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.

Petitioners being mother and brother of the deceased Danush.S,
were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole bread earning member in his family.
She has further deposed that, he has spent huge towards medicine, funeral and other expenses.

15. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased,
Petitioner No.2 is the brother of the said deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of herself and petitioner No.2.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased Danush.S.
Since, the respondents have not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer ISSUE No.2 In the affirmative.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 22 years.
As per the aadhar card marked, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 16.05.2002, the accident was occurred on 03.04.2024.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 22 years.
(ii).Income of the deceased:
According to the petitioners deceased was painter and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, the petitioner has not any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

17. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

19. Loss of dependency: The following Points are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

22. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:-
In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.20,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
